newsitem.title: MEXICO: LMX to start Mexico silver, lead, zinc operation.
newsitem.headline: LMX to start Mexico silver, lead, zinc operation.

text.p: LMX Resources Ltd will start ore production at its silver-lead-zinc project in Mexico this year, a senior vice-president of the Vancouver company said here Monday.

Peter J. Hawley told the Mexican Mining 1997 conference that the company planned a 300-tonne-per-day extraction at its Vianey project in the state of Guerrero. He gave no specific start up date and did not specify metal production targets.

Hawley said the production rate would give a net profit of $3-$5 million per year and added the mine had a mining reserve life of 11 years. He said the company planned to contract the ore out to a nearby miller.

Hawley said LMX had discovered vein widths ranging from 31 to 10 meters, silver grades of between 7.61 ounces per tonne to 1.67 ounces per tonne, lead contents of 1.99 percent to 0.75 percent and zinc contents of 6.94 percent to 1.08 percent.
"These are not the best holes, they are the ones I chose as examples," he said.
The Vianey mine property is close to the town of Mezcala in the central mountains south of Mexico City.
